scope: Independent single-batch review of eight original saved whole screenshots, visible pixels only.

visiblePixels: The title and printed-page line are separated from the opening prose; paragraphs remain inside a centered column with clear line spacing.
The derivation's stacked fractions, equation numbers, and following paragraphs have visible separation rather than overlapping baselines or cut-off right ends.

The ray diagram is fully framed with whitespace above and below. Its object/image arrows, central vertical line, and nearby labels are visible; the dense outgoing arrowheads do not cover the adjacent image-point label.
The Lens Magnification heading, bold definition, later formulas, and bottom Exercises button are visible without colliding.
limits: Small fraction characters and diagram subscripts are not an exact glyph transcription or a measured minimum-text-size certification.
Diagram observations concern framing and label separation, not scientific relationships or source fidelity.

visiblePixels: The long exercise title fits across the top without touching the printed-page line or Questions heading.
All eight numbered prompts are visible in distinct rows with horizontal separators; the text stays clear of the rules and right margin.
The Back to text button sits below the last question with a visible gap and an unclipped label.
limits: The button's visible appearance does not establish navigation or keyboard behavior.
Question wording and scientific correctness were not re-reviewed.

The early inline equations and the standalone fraction equation in answer 6 fit the column without entering neighboring prose.
Answer 7's numbered ray descriptions wrap on separate lines within the column, and answer 8's final paragraph remains visible above the bottom whitespace.
Section rules do not intersect text, and no definite clipping or overlap is visible.
limits: The long whole screenshot supports layout observations, not exhaustive transcription of small subscripts.
Answers were not solved or checked for semantics.

visiblePixels: Question groups 1 through 8 are visible with rules between groups, and circular or square controls occupy a separate left column from option letters and text.
Question 2's long formula rows visibly extend through their right-hand relations within the desktop option area, without abrupt cut-off at its edge.
Long options in the critical-angle and thin-lens groups wrap onto separated continuation lines rather than overlapping another option.
The lower formula options and the final question's options fit the visible column with bottom whitespace after the last row.
limits: Control shape and placement do not certify selection, judging, or accessibility behavior.
The tall screenshot does not support exact transcription of every small mathematical glyph; option correctness was not re-reviewed.

visiblePixels: The title wraps into two lines above the page metadata. Body prose wraps within visible left and right gutters without a word visibly crossing the page edge.
The derivation's display equations and equation numbers stay inside the narrow text column; surrounding prose remains vertically separated.

The bold magnification definition wraps across several lines; the concluding paragraph and Exercises button remain visible with clear spacing.
limits: The diagram is visibly smaller than its desktop counterpart; exact subscript shapes and numeric text-size thresholds are not certified.
No scrolling, geometry correctness, or unseen responsive state is inferred.

visiblePixels: The exercise title wraps into two lines and stays inside the visible right edge, with the page metadata below it.
All eight numbered questions are visible. Longer questions 2, 3, and 7 wrap onto continuation lines with their separators below the completed text.
The blue Questions marker does not touch its label, and the Back to text button is fully visible below question 8.
limits: This static view does not certify the button's action or a complete interactive exercise workflow.

visiblePixels: The title wraps above the Answers heading, and all eight numbered answer sections are visible with consistent outer gutters.
Inline equations in the early sections fit their lines or move with the prose; the display fraction in answer 6 remains inside the column.
The long numbered descriptions in answer 7 wrap without touching the section divider or answer 8.
Answer 8's inline magnification expressions and final explanatory lines are visibly separated and are not cut off by the bottom boundary.
limits: These are visible wrapping and spacing observations, not a complete small-glyph or English-accessibility certification.
Scientific meaning and answer correctness remain outside this review.

visiblePixels: The title and Choices heading wrap cleanly, and question groups 1 through 8 are visible with separated control and option-letter columns.
In question 2, each of options A, B, C, and D has a long formula line whose right-hand continuation is abruptly cut off at the same option-content right edge.

The blank page gutter remains visible to the right of those cut-off formula lines. This is local content-edge clipping within the saved screenshot, not merely content meeting the screenshot's outer boundary.

Question 2 option C has a separate prose continuation below its clipped formula. In the other visible question groups, long prose and shorter formulas wrap into separated lines without a comparable definite cut-off.
The final question's options and lower whitespace are visible; no additional definite overlap is identified.
limits: The tool reported automatic display resizing from 390x8279 to 283x6000. No additional image, crop, zoom, or reopened view was requested.
The abrupt common right-edge termination is visible despite that reduction, but the exact clipped small glyphs are not transcribed.
The saved pixels do not establish the clipping's implementation cause or whether horizontal scrolling could reveal the missing continuation.

findings.affectedArea: Question 2, options A-D, the right ends of the long formula rows.
findings.visibleDefect: All four formula rows lose their right-hand continuation at the option-content edge while the outer right page gutter is still visible. The saved mobile surface therefore does not display those rows in full.
findings.impact: The learner cannot read the complete displayed relations from this saved mobile view.
findings.requiredOutcome: Make the affected formula continuations visibly readable on the mobile choices surface without cut-off, then obtain affected-only saved-pixel review of the changed candidate.
findings.limits: No exact missing-glyph transcription, content correction, DOM diagnosis, or assertion about horizontal-scroll behavior.

staticViewLimits: Only the eight designated original screenshot paths were opened, each exactly once in this fresh context. No other images, reopens, crops, zooms, or derived images were used.
Inputs copy the manifest's image metadata; image bytes and hashes were not independently recomputed during this pixel-only review.
A saved viewport boundary is an evidence limit, not automatic proof of a broken container. The reported defect instead has a visible outer page gutter beyond the local formula cut-off.
No browser, native UI, renderer, network, database, paid service, Git, or product-edit operations were performed.
Source, science, English, choice semantics, native, and DOM approvals are reused as supplied, not re-reviewed or independently recertified.

This review does not certify interaction, judging, keyboard behavior, scrolling or scroll endpoints, ARIA, complete English accessibility, font identity or loading, unseen states, or headed acceptance.
Visible layout was judged at the supplied tool presentation. No precise minimum font-size measurement or exhaustive small-glyph transcription is claimed.
closesReadyScope: This saved-pixel review is complete, but its acceptance gate is not closes-ready: the mobile question-2 formula clipping requires revision. This is not a ticket-closure certification.
